notes: Legacy F/A-18C proportions anchored to NASA three-view and US Navy photographs; approximately 17.07 m length and 11.43 m bare wing span.
Visual reconstruction for rendering. Internal structure, loads, certified materials, exact hinges and motion limits are not engineering data.
VFA-146/CVW-9 NG identity is historical for Stennis circa 2009. The NG301 low-visibility markings are an original interpretation, not a museum-exact BuNo reconstruction.
Default HALF-flap launch appearance: approximately 12 degrees leading-edge and 30 degrees trailing-edge droop; joints are artistic animation controls.

Landing gear rebuilt with public NAVAIR tire nominal sizes, original trailing-arm/oleo geometry, aft main and forward nose retraction, linked main shrink and wheel planing. True passive coplanar linkage loops are used. Small pivot/actuator dimensions and timing are visual approximations, not aircraft engineering.

RC3 cockpit rebuild: DDI 163.5125 x 172.72 mm, AMPCD 167.005 x 182.6228 mm, UFC main face 173.0375 x 114.3 mm, upper central face 535.94 x 230.1875 mm; dimensions measured from OpenHornet public manufacturing reference envelopes at commit 77c7b2c07240d9d6062c16ed6e533bf2ed8bfce6. All meshes, panel outlines, labels and symbology are original; no OpenHornet/DCS paths, meshes or textures imported. Instrument face relocated to x4.75 m for realistic seat-to-panel reach; authentic named console families replace generic repeated panels. Includes instrument backs, connector hardware, cable looms, removable lining, photo-informed NACES seat and poseable controls. Internal electronics are visible illustrative packaging; no avionics simulation or certified aircraft wiring schematic.
Revision 2 replaces opaque intake blockers and intersecting filled fuselage lofts with continuous hollow ducts and segmented finite-thickness outer skins.

Primary Legacy-family structure references support metal spars/ribs, composite wing skins, center-barrel wing/main-gear load paths, dorsal decks and keel longerons. Exact station spacing and gauges are original visual reconstruction.
Four fuselage fuel-cell envelopes, one vent cell and wet-wing pipework follow publicly documented architecture; capacity, exact routing, fittings and bay subdivisions are not certified dimensions.
Inspectable skin, duct, fuel-cell, equipment and structure groups are independently named; inspection variants preserve the complete closed model in the master.
F404 geometry: GE family datasheet -402 overall 154 in length, 28 in inlet diameter, 35 in maximum envelope; source inches converted to metres.
Both F404 assemblies contain three fan stages, seven HPC stages, one HPT and one LPT; N1 fan/LPT and N2 HPC/HPT are separate concentric native revolute assemblies.
Engine blade counts, profiles, internal stations, bearings, accessory routing and small hardware are original visual approximations; not production drawings or engineering tolerances.

The 12-sector nozzle uses primary/divergent flap hinges and interleaved seals, mechanically coupled in native RC3 to a common slider; its ±25 mm demonstration stroke and linear ratios are authored, not an engine operating schedule.
Engine combustor and afterburner liner holes are open three-dimensional bores. Casing and liner quadrant sliders permit physical inspection cutaways.

Fan inlet and HPC inlet/first two stator rows contain individually pitchable guide vanes, coupled to fan and HPC control-ring drives. Vane counts and the 12:1 demonstration ratio are authored visual parameters.

Titanium is assigned where public family references support it. Built-in Stainless Steel is the closest available hot-section alloy proxy; no Nickel or Inconel built-in material exists in verified RC3.
This is an articulated visual engine assembly. Rotation and nozzle kinematics do not simulate combustion, thrust, gas dynamics, engine controls, or engineering performance.

Cockpit links are geometric demonstration couplings, not F/A-18 FLCS, avionics or engine-control simulation. Stick pitch drives both stabilators; left pedal counter-drives the right pedal and drives rudders/NWS; flap selector drives TE/LE only; gear, hook and wingfold handles drive their assemblies. Ailerons follow stick roll around the 30-degree launch droop, within 15.6..44.4 degrees. Automatic aileron/flap mixing is intentionally omitted because the tested RC3 coaxial stop loop displaced the other input. Engine shaft/nozzle/variable-geometry motions remain separately inspectable.

CVN-74 is an original photo-informed visual reconstruction at Nimitz-class overall scale, not a surveyed ship model. Detail is concentrated near catapult one and the island. Deck offset, surface wear, equipment and historic radar fit are interpretive.

The four catapult-one JBD panels and two radar arrays have native revolute joints. Four separate elevator platforms have vertical slider joints (metres in this source, travel -10 to 0); their machinery and realistic constraints are not simulated. Four static original deck-crew figures have no real-person likeness.
Catapult-one shuttle engagement is centred at x=4.71 m, y=0, z=0.09 m to meet the aircraft launch-bar cross pin in the launch preset. Its geometry is visual, not engineered launching hardware.
